newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan household spending drop less than feared-EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan household spending drop less than feared-EPA.

text.p: A real year-on-year decline of 1.0 percent in Japan's April household spending, announced on Thursday, was within expectations or slightly smaller than expected, Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told a regular news conference on Friday.
He said that an EPA survey had shown that most industry sectors expected the fall-off in consumer spending, after the April 1 rise in the sales tax, to have run its course by the end of June.

Asked about the effects of fiscal tightening on the economy, Aso said he was well aware that the economy could slow in the short term, adding that while private demand was firm, it was a sector that needed to be watched.
He added that if private demand were to weaken, there may be pressure not to raise interest rates.
Stating that the economy was "a living organism", he said there were many factors to consider when assessing the economy, such as the dollar/yen rate and the effects of deregulation.
